bib.title: LongHarness: Advancing Agentic Reasoning over 100M-Token Corpora via Stateful Evidence Management

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "LongHarness: Advancing Agentic Reasoning over 100M-Token Corpora via Stateful Evidence Management." Songtao Huang, Zhijie Zhong, et al. (corresponding author Shiyang Feng), Shanghai AI Laboratory and several universities. arXiv:2610.13075v1 [cs.AI], 9 Oct 2026. Preprint. No peer-reviewed venue is shown.

COVERAGE: All 19 pages read, 70,620 chars, including Appendices A–E and the Table 9 repeated runs. The extraction is clean. I skimmed the reference list for origins. The prompt text in Appendix B is partly truncated in the extraction.

**Fit.** This is partly off-topic for note 06. It is a retrieval and evidence-state harness for corpus QA, not a session-lifecycle paper. It has no session lifecycle, no progress files, no compaction versus reset comparison, no Ralph loop and no entropy management. It touches 06 only through "state externalization": structured persistent state outside the interaction history. It is weaker as a source on long-horizon execution than on state design. It is a closer fit for `02-harness-anatomy`, or for a note on context or memory design (02-context-engineering notes 06 and 11). Cite it in 06 only as narrow evidence that structured external state beats the plain interaction history and beats free-text notes. 07 orchestration and 08 maturity do not fit, because it is a single agent.

**Core claim.** Keeping evidence (a source-linked EvidenceBank) and conclusions (a Conclusion State with explicit unresolved gaps) as separate persistent states, outside the history, curbs "unbounded exploration" and "evidence-state drift." Superseded or retracted evidence is revised explicitly, not appended.

**Headline numbers.** All main-table figures are one run per setting.
- GLM-5.3-Flash, OfficeQA Pro exact match: direct 15.8 to 60.2 on V1 (133 questions, ~100M tokens, 697 documents) and 4.4 to 61.1 on V2 (90 questions, 1,435 documents).
  - Direct baselines get BM25 passages in a 256K-token window.
  - The best competing harness scores 48.1 on V1 (Claude Code) and 42.2 on V2 (Codex).
  - Steps and limits: LongHarness gets 200 steps, a 1M-token cumulative read budget and 60 searches. Codex and Claude Code get 200 turns and 200 tool calls. RLM gets 30 iterations.
- Qwen3.8-Flash: 61.7 on V1 (Claude Code 53.4) and 51.1 on V2 (Codex 50.0, so the margin is only 1.1 points).
- Average across the four benchmarks: 70.3 for LongHarness against 58.8 for Codex (GLM). With Qwen it is 69.2 against 62.5.
- AA-LCR (100 questions): 84.0 (GLM) and 87.0 (Qwen). LongBench v2 Long (108 questions): 75.9 and 76.9.
- Turn counts (median, V1 to V2): LongHarness 22 to 30, Claude Code 21 to 116, Codex 19 to 43. Codex exhausts its turn budget on 3.8% of V1 and 21.1% of V2 questions.
- Three-run results (GLM-5.3-Flash, Table 9, App. D, p19):
  - V1: LongHarness mean 59.90 (std 0.43) against Claude Code 49.37.
  - V2: LongHarness 59.63 (std 1.28) against Codex 41.11 (std 4.00).
  - AA-LCR: LongHarness 84.00 against Claude Code 80.33.
- Cost: no dollar, token or wall-clock cost is reported, only turn counts and budgets.

**Ablation (Table 2, GLM-5.3-Flash, one run, exact match, p7).** Full is 60.2 on V1 and 61.1 on V2.

| Variant | V1 | V2 |
|---|---|---|
| w/o Persistent States (history only) | 55.6 | 53.3 |
| w/o Coevolution | 54.9 | 51.7 |
| Naive append-only evidence | 56.4 | 51.1 |
| w/o explicit conclusion-guided exploration instruction | 55.6 | 53.3 |
| Generic free-text working notes | 53.4 | 53.3 |

All five drop 3.8–10.0 points, and all drop more on V2. Each ablated variant still scores far above the direct baselines, and the gap to Claude Code and Codex on V1 is within about 8 points. So much of the gain over those harnesses comes from the shared search, bounded-read and compute scaffold, not only from the state design.

**Trajectory audit (Table 3, p7).** An LLM auditor (GPT-5.6-Luna) classifies failures. On V2, retrieval, editing and transformation success are 87.8, 87.3 and 79.7 for LongHarness. Claude Code is 76.7, 78.3 and 70.4 per the extracted columns, though the column alignment is ambiguous.

**Quotes.**
- "Reasoning, actions, and observations accumulate in the history, while evidence and conclusions persist across turns." (§2.4, p5)
- "Superseding or retracting evidence does not automatically rewrite dependent conclusions." (§2.4, p5)
- "Due to computational resource constraints, the main comparison uses one run per harness and evaluation setting." (§3.1, p5–6)
- "Codex ... making 103 consecutive backward reads (unbounded exploration)... recognizes the corrected value 4400 but retains the earlier result in its final answer." (App. E, p19)

**Limits.**
- There is no limitations section.
- The main table is single-run. Only the GLM backbone has repeated runs, and the V2 sets are small (90 questions).
- It compares harnesses only on QA benchmarks, not on multi-session or software tasks. It never tests compaction, context reset or session handoff.
- Baselines are not matched in tooling. The authors' harness gets purpose-built search and read tools, while Codex and Claude Code use a shell.
- The Qwen V2 margin is 1.1 points.
- The failure audit is by an LLM (GPT-5.6-Luna), and the AA-LCR grader is also GPT-5.6-Luna.
- Direct AA-LCR scores come from Artificial Analysis, not from this paper's own runs. Direct baselines get BM25 retrieval, which is a weak comparator.
- The case study is one trajectory, chosen at random from Codex failures.
- The text offers its turn-count explanation only as "a plausible explanation."
- The model names are releases I cannot verify.

**Builds on.**
- ReAct (Yao et al., 2023).
- Recursive language models (Zhang et al., 2025).
- Prime Agent (Karten et al., 2026).
- MemWalker (Chen et al., 2023).
- ReadAgent (Lee et al., 2024).
- MemGPT (Packer et al., 2024, listed under "persistent memory"; the attribution is an inference).
- LedgerMind (Du et al., 2026) and SLIDERS (Joshi et al., 2026), for evidence ledgers.
- Cao et al., 2026 (arXiv 2603.20432), for coding agents as long-context processors.
- It reuses OfficeQA Pro (Opsahl-Ong et al., 2026).

**Figure candidate.** Figure 4 (p8): "Evidence lifecycle comparison with GLM-5.3-Flash on OfficeQA Pro V1." Codex takes 170 steps and loses a correction. LongHarness takes 10 steps and carries the revision through. Figure 2 (p4) is the architecture alternative.

**Problems.** No embedded instructions found. The Table 3 columns are jumbled in the extraction. The Appendix B.3 prompt text is partly cut in the extracted output.
